newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso trims gains, banks exercise dlr puts.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso trims gains, banks exercise dlr puts.

text.p: The Mexican peso curtailed some earlier firmness at the close on Tuesday after banks chose to exercise some dollar puts with the central bank, dealers said.
Nonetheless, the peso was still strong on foreign investment flows, they added.
"Dollar liquidity in the market was definitely due to real foreign investment flows to the bourse," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both ended 0.6 of a centavo firmer at 7.8050/7.8090 and 7.8030/7.8060 per dollar, respectively.
Banco de Mexico stepped up its month-end dollar put auction on July 31 to $500 million pesos in what many analysts saw as a move to curb recent peso strength.
Dealers estimated banks exercised $225 million of those puts during Tuesday's session.
According to Banco de Mexico procedures, if 80 percent of puts were exercised by mid-month, the central bank could hold an additional auction for another $500 million.
"The peso moved little today because banks exercised dollar put auctions," another trader said.
Same-day peso contracts had closed mid-morning 2.4 centavos firmer at 7.7980/7.8010 per dollar.
Dealers said the peso could retain its current strength on Wednesday if interest rates gained at the central bank primary auction later in the day.

A Reuters survey of nine money market traders showed they forecast Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at an average of 18.45 percent. This would be a rise of 75 basis points since last week.
